module_title: Chemical Classification: Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures
introduction: While physical states (solid, liquid, gas) tell us how matter looks and behaves mechanically, chemical classification tells us what matter is actually made of at the fundamental atomic level.

core_concepts.title: Pure Substances: Elements
core_concepts.description:
An element is a basic form of matter that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions. It consists of only ONE single type of atom. 
Types: 
1. Metals (e.g., Gold, Iron, Copper). 
2. Non-metals (e.g., Oxygen, Carbon, Chlorine). 
3. Metalloids (e.g., Silicon, Germanium - showing intermediate properties of both).

core_concepts.title: Pure Substances: Compounds
core_concepts.description:
A substance composed of TWO or MORE elements, chemically combined with one another in a strictly fixed proportion by mass. 
Properties: The properties of a compound are entirely different from its constituent elements. Example: Water (H2O) puts out fire, but its constituents Hydrogen (highly explosive gas) and Oxygen (supporter of combustion) behave completely differently.

core_concepts.title: Mixtures
core_concepts.description:
Substances composed of two or more elements or compounds that are mixed together physically, NOT chemically. The ratio is not fixed, and no new substance is formed. 
1. Homogeneous Mixture: Uniform composition throughout (e.g., Salt dissolved in water, clean Air, Alloys like Brass). 
2. Heterogeneous Mixture: Non-uniform composition with distinct boundaries (e.g., Sand and salt, Oil and water, Blood).

core_concepts.title: Triple Point
core_concepts.description: The unique, precise temperature and pressure at which all three phases of a substance (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in perfect thermodynamic equilibrium. For water, the triple point is exactly 0.01°C at a pressure of 0.006 atm.

important_entities.name: Alloys are Mixtures
important_entities.significance: Examiners often trick students by asking if an alloy (like Steel, Bronze, or Brass) is a compound. It is NOT. An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and non-metal) because it retains the properties of its constituent metals and its composition can be varied.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Is Air a compound? NO. Air is a homogeneous mixture of various unbonded gases (N2, O2, Ar, CO2). You can separate air by physical means (fractional distillation). Water (H2O) is a compound and can ONLY be separated by chemical means (electrolysis).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Compounds are Married, Mixtures are just Roommates
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Compounds are chemically bonded (married) and create a totally new identity. Mixtures just share the same space (roommates) and keep their own individual identities.

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS Exams frequently ask you to identify metalloids from a list. Memorize the major ones: Boron (B), Silicon (Si), Germanium (Ge), Arsenic (As), Antimony (Sb).
